# Hall Safety Rules
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

## 1. Scope
1.1 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.
1.2 They apply to all hirers, trustees, visitors and contractors.
1.3 The named hirer must explain emergency exits to organisers.

## 2. Fire safety
2.1 All marked fire exits must remain unobstructed.
2.2 Fire doors must not be wedged open.
2.3 Open flames, candles and fireworks are prohibited.
2.4 Electrical appliances brought in must be safe and undamaged.
2.5 Cooking is permitted only in the designated kitchen.
2.6 No cooking equipment may be placed in hired rooms.

## 3. Occupancy and supervision
3.1 Maximum numbers are specified in hall-bookings.md section 4.
3.2 The hirer must count attendees when an event begins.
3.3 Children under 12 must remain under adult supervision.
3.4 At least one responsible adult must remain near the main entrance.
3.5 Corridors and access routes must remain clear.

## 4. Emergencies and reporting
4.1 In a fire, occupants must evacuate immediately.
4.2 Emergency services must be contacted when necessary.
4.3 Occupants must assemble at the marked garden gate.
4.4 Nobody may re-enter until emergency services permit it.
4.5 Injuries requiring first aid must be recorded in the incident book.
4.6 Serious incidents must be reported to the chair within 24 hours.

## 5. Emergency spending
5.1 The chair may authorise up to £400 for urgent safety work.
5.2 This exception overrides hall-trustees.md section 5.2.
5.3 A second trustee must confirm the urgency in writing.
5.4 The spending must be reported at the next committee meeting.

## 6. Temporary closure
6.1 The chair may close an unsafe room immediately.
6.2 A closed room must not be hired until declared safe.
6.3 Refunds caused by safety closure follow hall-refunds.md section 3.

6	# Room Booking Rules
7	Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.
8	
9	## 1. General conditions
10	1.1 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.
11	1.2 Rooms may be hired by adults aged 18 or over.
12	1.3 The named hirer is responsible for the entire booking.
13	1.4 The hirer must give a contact address and telephone number.
14	
15	## 2. Booking requests
16	2.1 Requests may be submitted up to 12 months in advance.
17	2.2 Requests must arrive at least three calendar days before the event.
18	2.3 The booking officer checks availability before accepting a request.
19	2.4 A booking is accepted only when written acceptance is issued.
20	2.5 Payment deadlines are set out in hall-fees.md section 6.
21	2.6 Failure to pay the booking deposit cancels an accepted booking.
22	
23	## 3. Opening hours
24	3.1 Monday to Thursday: 08:00 to 22:00.
25	3.2 Friday and Saturday: 08:00 to 23:00.
26	3.3 Sunday: 09:00 to 21:00.
27	3.4 All guests must leave by the relevant closing time.
28	3.5 Setup and clearing must take place within booked hours.
29	
30	## 4. Room capacities
31	4.1 Main Hall: maximum 90 people.
32	4.2 Meeting Room: maximum 24 people.
33	4.3 Combined events may not exceed 100 people in the building.
34	4.4 Capacities include organisers, performers and children.
35	4.5 Fire safety requirements in hall-safety.md also apply.
36	
37	## 5. Access and equipment
38	5.1 Keys are collected from the booking officer by arrangement.
39	5.2 Keys may not be copied or passed to another hirer.
40	5.3 Equipment must be requested when the booking is made.
41	5.4 Equipment charges follow hall-fees.md section 4.
42	5.5 Hirers must report missing or faulty equipment before use.
43	
44	## 6. Changes
45	6.1 Changes to dates or rooms require written approval.
46	6.2 A date change counts as cancellation and a new booking.
47	6.3 Cancellation charges are governed by hall-refunds.md.

# Room Booking Rules
Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.

1.1 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.
1.2 Rooms may be hired by adults aged 18 or over.
1.3 The named hirer is responsible for the entire booking.
1.4 The hirer must give a contact address and telephone number.

2.1 Requests may be submitted up to 12 months in advance.
2.2 Requests must arrive at least three calendar days before the event.
2.3 The booking officer checks availability before accepting a request.
2.4 A booking is accepted only when written acceptance is issued.
2.5 Payment deadlines are set out in hall-fees.md section 6.
2.6 Failure to pay the booking deposit cancels an accepted booking.

3.1 Monday to Thursday: 08:00 to 22:00.
3.2 Friday and Saturday: 08:00 to 23:00.
3.3 Sunday: 09:00 to 21:00.
3.4 All guests must leave by the relevant closing time.
3.5 Setup and clearing must take place within booked hours.

4.2 Meeting Room: maximum 24 people.
4.3 Combined events may not exceed 100 people in the building.
4.4 Capacities include organisers, performers and children.
4.5 Fire safety requirements in hall-safety.md also apply.

5.2 Keys may not be copied or passed to another hirer.

6	# Trustee Committee Rules
7	Quillbrook Village Hall is a fictional organisation.
8	
9	## 1. Purpose
10	1.1 The committee manages the hall for community use.
11	1.2 It may hire out rooms and equipment under hall-bookings.md.
12	1.3 These rules were adopted on 12 February 2025.
13	
14	## 2. Committee membership
15	2.1 The committee has between five and nine trustees.
16	2.2 Trustees must be at least 18 years old.
17	2.3 Applicants must live in Quillbrook or a neighbouring village.
18	2.4 A trustee serves for two years and may stand again.
19	2.5 Trustees receive no payment for committee work.
20	
21	## 3. Appointment and departure
22	3.1 New trustees are elected at the annual public meeting.
23	3.2 Election requires more than half of votes cast.
24	3.3 The committee may fill vacancies until the next annual meeting.
25	3.4 A trustee may resign by giving written notice.
26	3.5 Three consecutive missed meetings without explanation trigger a review.
27	
28	## 4. Meetings and votes
29	4.1 The committee meets at least six times each calendar year.
30	4.2 Four trustees form a quorum.
31	4.3 Decisions require a majority of those present and voting.
32	4.4 The chair has a casting vote if votes are equal.
33	4.5 Minutes must be approved at the next meeting.
34	
35	## 5. Spending authority
36	5.1 The treasurer may approve routine spending up to £150.
37	5.2 Spending above £150 requires a committee vote.
38	5.3 Emergency safety spending follows hall-safety.md section 5.
39	5.4 Two trustees must approve payments above £500.
40	
41	## 6. Matters not covered
42	6.1 These rules do not set a maximum number of trustee terms.
43	6.2 They do not prescribe a method for resolving personal disputes.
44	6.3 They do not specify whether trustees may attend remotely.
